correctness.rationale: A unit rank-one map factors as Tz=ℓ(z)u with both factors unit. Along the interior of a primal edge the only norming functional is its support, and the absolute pairing is bounded by endpoint values; at each vertex the norming segment has just the two adjacent supports as extreme points. This gives formula (1) over ten vertex-support pairs of edges. The cosine row (1,1,r,0,−r,−1,−1,−r,0,r) follows from the angle differences, with r²=1−r. Rotate and reflect u onto the first half-edge so 0≤s≤1/2, and change the sign of ℓ to cover the five dual edges. For j=0,1,3,4 the common vertex immediately gives bounds 1, r+r²s, 1−r²s>r, 1, respectively. For j=2 the bounds from v_2,v_4 are positive and vary strictly in opposite directions with t, crossing at t=s with value r+r⁴s(1−s). Equality therefore requires s=0; for j=2 it forces t=0, and for j=1 the v_1 test forces t=1. Both give ℓ=q_2. At (v_0,q_2) the maximum is r by the exact row. Reflection about v_0 sends the perpendicular q_2 to −q_2, so undoing symmetries gives exactly ±T_i modulo the five distinct range lines. q_{i+2}(v_i)=0 gives square-zero, and the cited ordinary-index theorem gives r/2. The supporting checker.py was inspected; its finite sampling is not used to infer the universal bound or rigidity.

value.rationale: The regular decagon is a natural test beyond the inspected hexagonal and octagonal rank-one families. The exact ratio to the known full index isolates the effect of restricting to rank one, and complete square-zero rigidity identifies the actual minimizers rather than merely producing a numerical bound or one candidate. This is a useful exact invariant and structural classification without claiming a general polygon theorem.
